rv.q: Their production marries the clear-eyed humour and sadness of the writing to a deeply felt sense of empathy and authenticity.
But plot twists fly out of nowhere towards the end, turning this into melodrama rather than mood piece.

It’s small, quiet moments like these where the play really shines, where the raw emotion of McCraney's storytelling shines a light on the complex nuances of the struggles these characters face in their journey towards adulthood.
This beautiful, joyous play rejoices in all that it means to march to your own drum.
Playwright McCraney and director Nancy Medina have created an impactful and hopeful show that deserves to be shared.
When he lifts his head, when he takes pride in himself and his difference, both he and Choir Boy soar.
It occasionally leads us down a dead end, but the chemistry and closeness that are obvious in the cast keep us invested.
Choir Boy has charm and wit, and there’s plenty about which you can sing your praises, but it lacks a certain energy to capitalise on its warmth and tenderness.
Overall, Choir Boy is a fantastically performed, written and directed coming-of-age piece of theatre.
Choir Boy has the power to fill hearts with joy.

cn.t: McCraney's moving coming-of-age story about a gay Black student at an elite prep school earns praise for its powerful performances, beautiful spirituals, and emotional resonance, though some find the pacing uneven.
